questions.question: Bharatanatyam has originated from which of these states?
questions.questionHtml: Bharatanatyam has originated from which of these states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

Key Points

  • Bharatanatyam is a classical Indian dance form that originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
  • It is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India, with its roots tracing back to the ancient Tamil culture.
  • Bharatanatyam combines expressive dance (abhinaya) with rhythmic footwork (nritta) to convey religious and mythological stories.
  • The dance form is typically performed by a solo dancer and is accompanied by Carnatic music.

Additional Information

  • Origin of Bharatanatyam:
    • Bharatanatyam originated in the Hindu temples of Tamil Nadu and was initially performed by devadasis (temple dancers).
    • The dance form's history can be traced back to the Natya Shastra, an ancient treatise on performing arts written by the sage Bharata.
    • It was later codified and standardized in the 19th and 20th centuries by notable dance gurus such as Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.
  • Structure of a Bharatanatyam Performance:
    • A typical Bharatanatyam performance consists of a series of dances, including Alarippu (invocation), Jatiswaram (pure dance), Shabdam (expressive dance), Varnam (narrative dance), Padams (lyrical dance), and Tillana (concluding dance).
    • Each segment showcases the dancer's technical prowess, emotional expression, and storytelling ability.
  • Costume and Makeup:
    • Bharatanatyam dancers wear traditional costumes, usually consisting of a saree draped in a distinctive style that allows for freedom of movement.
    • The makeup includes intricate facial designs, expressive eye makeup, and jewelry that enhances the dancer's expressions and movements.
  • Significance of Bharatanatyam:
    • Bharatanatyam is not just a dance form but a spiritual practice that conveys stories from Hindu mythology and religious themes.
    • It plays a crucial role in preserving and promoting Indian cultural heritage and is performed at various cultural festivals and events worldwide.

questions.question: Which among the following dance form was originally performed in the temples of Tamil Nadu, by the Devadasis and therefore it is also known as Dasiattam?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following dance form was originally performed in the temples of Tamil Nadu, by the Devadasis and therefore it is also known as Dasiattam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

Key Points

  • Bharatnatyam
    • Bharatanatyam of Tamil Nadu in Southern India has grown out of the art of dancers dedicated to temples and was earlier known as Sadir or Dasi Attam.
    • It is the first of India's traditional dances to be refashioned by theatre artists and to be exhibited widely both at home and abroad.
    • Bharatanatyam rests on principles of performance and aesthetics set down in classics such as Bharata's Natyashastra.
    • It has a rich repertoire of songs in Telugu, Tamil, and Sanskrit.
    • The music of Bharatanatyam belongs to the Carnatic system of southern India.
    • The musicians accompanying a dance recital include at least one vocalist, a Mridangam (drum)-player, a flutist or violinist, or Veena (lute)-player.
    • The group also includes a Nattuvanar, or dance conductor, who recites the dance syllables as he plays a pair of small bronze cymbals.

questions.question: Which classical dance was introduced by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam?
questions.questionHtml: Which classical dance was introduced by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam?
questions.solution: Sattriya is a classical dance form from Assam introduced by the 15th-century Vaishnava saint and reformer Sankardev. This dance form artistically presents mythological teachings through a combination of dance, drama, and music, and is integral to Assamese culture. It is performed in Sattras (monasteries) as part of daily rituals and special festivals. Recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi as one of India's eight classical dance forms in 2000, Sattriya has a tradition spanning over 500 years. Sankardev, a pivotal figure in Assam's cultural and religious history, laid the foundation of the Bhakti movement in the region.

questions.question: Lachhu Maharaj is a celebrated ________ dancer.
questions.questionHtml: Lachhu Maharaj is a celebrated ________ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathak

Key Points

  • Lachhu Maharaj is a celebrated Kathak dancer.
  • Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
  • This dance form traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.
  • Kathak is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions, which are used to tell a story.
  • It has three main gharanas (schools) – Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras, each with its own unique style and emphasis.

Additional Information

  • Lachhu Maharaj (1901–1978), also known as Baij Nath Prasad, was a noted Kathak dancer and choreographer from the Banaras gharana.
  • He was honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Indian dance.
  • Lachhu Maharaj was known for his expressive abhinaya (acting) and delicate footwork.
  • He contributed significantly to the popularization and development of Kathak dance in India and abroad.
  • His legacy continues to inspire new generations of Kathak dancers.

questions.question: The ____________ maestros who revived the art form in the late 1940s include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta.

  • The maestros who revived the art form in the late 1940s include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta.
  • They played a crucial role in the revival of Odissi dance.
  • Odissi is one of the classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
  • Kelucharan Mohapatra is considered one of the greatest exponents of Odissi dance, and his contributions have been vital in popularizing the dance form globally.
  • Raghunath Dutta also significantly contributed to the resurgence and preservation of Odissi dance during the mid-20th century.

Additional Information

  • Odissi is characterized by its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculptural poses.
  • It is traditionally performed to the accompaniment of Odissi music, which is known for its rhythmic and melodic complexity.
  • The dance form has roots in the ancient temples of Odisha, where it was performed as a form of worship.
  • Today, Odissi is performed on stages worldwide and continues to be a vital part of India's cultural heritage.

questions.question: Pandit Birju Maharaj was a legendary _________ dancer, who opened his dance school ‘Kalashram’ in New Delhi.
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Birju Maharaj was a legendary _________ dancer, who opened his dance school ‘Kalashram’ in New Delhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathak.

Key Points

  • Pandit Birju Maharaj was a renowned exponent of Kathak, a classical dance form originating from Northern India.
  • He was born on February 4, 1938, and came from a family of Kathak dancers, including his father, Acchan Maharaj.
  • Birju Maharaj was known for his expressive storytelling, graceful movements, and intricate footwork.
  • He received several prestigious awards, including the Padma Vibhushan in 1986, for his contributions to Kathak.
  • In 1998, he established his dance school, 'Kalashram,' in New Delhi to promote and teach Kathak to future generations.

Additional Information

  • Kathak:
    • One of the eight major classical dance forms of India, known for its dramatic and expressive style.
    • The word 'Kathak' is derived from 'Katha,' meaning story, and the dance form involves storytelling through rhythmic and graceful movements.
  • Padma Vibhushan:
    • India's second-highest civilian award, given for exceptional and distinguished service in any field including art, literature, science, and public services.
  • Kalashram:
    • An institute founded by Pandit Birju Maharaj dedicated to the preservation and promotion of Kathak and other traditional arts.
    • Kalashram offers training in dance, music, and other performing arts, continuing the legacy of Kathak.
  • Footwork (Tatkaar):
    • One of the most distinctive features of Kathak, involving intricate and fast-paced foot movements, often synchronized with the tabla (drum).
  • Abhinaya:
    • A critical element in Kathak, referring to the art of expression through facial gestures, body language, and hand movements to convey emotions and stories.

questions.question: In classical dance, which of the following Rasa represents "anger"?
questions.questionHtml: <font style="vertical-align: inherit;"><font style="vertical-align: inherit;">In classical dance, which of the following Rasa represents "anger"?</font></font>
questions.solution: In classical Indian dance, "Raudra" represents anger and is one of the Navarasas, the nine essential emotions in Indian classical arts. Raudra Rasa is depicted through intense expressions like furrowed brows and wide eyes. The Navarasas, which also include Shringara (Love), Hasya (Humor), Karuna (Compassion), Veera (Courage), Bhayanaka (Fear), Bibhatsa (Disgust), Adbhuta (Wonder), and Shanta (Peace), are fundamental for dancers to express a wide range of emotions. Mastery of these Rasas, rooted in ancient texts like the Natyashastra, enhances the storytelling and emotional impact of dance performances.

questions.question: Which among the following dance forms of India is associated with Odisha?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following dance forms of India is associated with Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chhau.

Key Points

  • Chhau dance:-
    • It is a traditional dance form performed by men from Eastern India that enacts episodes from epics including Ramayana and Mahabharata. 
    • The main objective of this dance form is to celebrate martial arts.
    • Chhau dance can be classified into three divisions based on the place it is performed; Mayurbhanj Chau of Odisha, Seraikella Chau of Jharkhand, and Purulia Chau of Bengal.
    •  Chhau dance is intimately connected to regional festivals, notably the spring festival Chaitra Parva.

Additional Information

  • Kathak:- 
    • Kathak classical dance originated in Uttar Pradesh, specifically in the courts of the Mughal emperors in the 16th century.
    • The dance form combines elements of Hindu and Muslim cultures, and is known for its intricate footwork, graceful hand gestures, and facial expressions.
  • Bhangra:-
    • Bhangra is a lively and vibrant form of folk dance and music that originated from Punjab, a region in Northern India and Eastern Pakistan.
    • It traditionally celebrates the harvest season and the arrival of Vaisakhi.
  • Ghumar:-
    • Ghumar, also known as Ghoomar, is a traditional folk dance originating from the Indian state of Rajasthan.
    • The dance is primarily performed by women and is known for its graceful movements and vibrant attire.

questions.question: ‘Jat-Jatin’, ‘Jhijhian Dance’ are popular folk dances of _________.
questions.questionHtml: ‘Jat-Jatin’, ‘Jhijhian Dance’ are popular folk dances of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bihar.

Key Points

  • Jat-Jattin:
    • It is the most popular folk dance of North Bihar, especially in Mithila and Koshi region.
    • Jat-Jattin is the dance of women and is supposed to be performed on moonlit nights during the monsoons.
    • Grown-up girls and young housewives gather in the courtyard and, accompanied by a drum, dance from midnight to sunrise.
    • Men goes to far-off places to earn livelihood.
    • Jat-Jattin is a folk dance of the same emigrant husband accompanied by his spouse.
    • Apart from poverty and sorrow, this dance reflects a rainbow of the sweet and tender quarrel as well as some complaints between husband and wife.
    • The folk dance mocks to comfort the hurdles of life with a smile.
    • Through this dance, various other socially concerned topics like poverty, sorrow, love, arguments between lovers or husband and wife are also enacted.
    • In some versions, the performers wear masks to add a real picture.

Additional Information 

  • Following are some famous folks dance in Bihar:-
    • Jhijhian Dance
    • Kajari Dance
    • Sohar- Khilouna Dance
    • Holi Dance
    • Jhumri Dance
    • Launda Dance

questions.question: Cheraw Dance is a traditional dance form of which state?
questions.questionHtml: Cheraw Dance is a traditional dance form of which state?
questions.solution: Cheraw Dance, also known as the Bamboo Dance, is a traditional and oldest dance form of Mizoram. Performed during special occasions like bumper harvests, it involves rhythmic bamboo movements. Mizoram's other traditional dances include Khuallam and Sarlamkai. The state's capital is Aizawl, and it boasts rich cultural and natural heritage.

questions.question: ‘Paika’ is a traditional dance form associated with which Indian state?
questions.questionHtml: ‘Paika’ is a traditional dance form associated with which Indian state?
questions.solution: ‘Paika’ is a traditional dance form associated with Jharkhand. Paika dance is mainly performed by the Munda community. Paikas were a group of soldiers who sacrificed their lives for the safety of the kingdom.

questions.question: Jagoi is a major style of which of the following forms of Indian classical dance?
questions.questionHtml: Jagoi is a major style of which of the following forms of Indian classical dance?
questions.solution: Jagoi is a major style of Manipuri, which is one of the forms of Indian classical dance.Manipuri dance originated in the northeastern state of Manipur and is known for its graceful movements, delicate hand gestures, and vibrant costumes.

questions.question: The Natyanjali Dance Festival is held every year during the months of February - March in the city of:
questions.questionHtml: The Natyanjali Dance Festival is held every year during the months of February - March in the city of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chidambaram.

Key Points

  • Every February and March, Natyyanjali Dance Festival is held in Parakara, Chidambaram Temple, Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu (Natyanjali Dance Festival). This is a five-day festival that begins on the auspicious day of Mahashivratri.
  • Natyanjali is an annual dance festival commemorating the Hindu Lord Shiva.
  • It originated around 1981 and was initially a relatively dark event.
  • The current version lasts about 13 days, and various styles of classical dance forms provide artistic support to the god Nataraja.

questions.question: Dumhal is a famous folk dance of which of the following states or Union Territory?
questions.questionHtml: Dumhal is a famous folk dance of which of the following states or Union Territory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir.

  • Dumhal is a famous folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir.

Key Points

  • The Dumhal dance is the popular folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir.
  • This dance is only performed by the men of the Wattal tribe of the region.
  • It is presented on specific auspicious occasions in the tribe.
  • The songs on which the dancers perform are folk songs that are sung by them in chorus.
  • Rauf, Hikat, Mandjas, Kud Dandi Nach, and Damali are some other folk dances of Jammu and Kashmir

Additional Information

  • Pandav Nritya, Bhotia Dance, and Cholia Dance are the folk dances of Uttarakhand.
  • Saila Dance, Karma Dance, Sua Nacha, Pandavani, and Panthi Dance are the folk dances of Chhattisgarh.
  • Jawara, Matki, Aada, Khada Nach, Phulpati and Grida Dance are the folk dances of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: The ‘Lezim’ dance form is peculiar to which of the following states?
questions.questionHtml: The ‘Lezim’ dance form is peculiar to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

  • The ‘Lezim’ dance form is peculiar to Maharashtra states.

Key Points

  • Lezim is a group dance that is performed in formations of two or four in the villages of Maharashtra.
    • Lezim performed in colorful costumes, the dance involves a dholki and all the dancers carry Lezim which an instrument with jingling cymbals.
    • It is often played during the Ganesh festival.
    • Other important dances of Maharashtra: Lavani, Nakata, Koli, Gafa, Dahikala.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is in UNESCO's Intangible Heritage List?

questions.solution: Chhau dance included in UNESCO's Intangible Heritage list in the year 2010. Chhau, a unique form of masked dance, is preserved by the royal family of Saraikela, the former state of Jharkhand.
